pure-announcement.rationale: An argumentative essay on memory ownership and lock-in; the Deep Agents pitch at the end is a coda, not the substance.

duplicate.rationale: Context-layer is about assembling task context, not about who owns agent memory; no nearest concept covers the harness-memory lock-in argument.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The load-bearing claims (stateful Responses API, Claude Managed Agents, Codex's encrypted compaction summaries) are sourced and independently checkable.

durability.rationale: The mechanism — memory is a harness capability because managing context is the harness's job, so closed or API-hosted harnesses convert accumulated state into provider lock-in — is a trade-off argument that holds regardless of which products currently illustrate it.

actionability.rationale: It yields a concrete decision rule — before adopting a harness or stateful API, check where session and long-term state physically lives, because switching cost compounds with accumulated memory — which changes vendor and architecture choices.

atomicity.rationale: One argument, stated in the note's own abstract: if you don't own the harness you don't own the memory, and memory is what creates lock-in.
